tagline: For the urban nomad who needs to flee a bad date *and* carry their dignity. This folding skateboard doubles as a backpack, so you can bail on a boring dinner, then pretend you were just out for a casual stroll. Perfect for when your 'I’m just popping out for a second' turns into a full-blown escape mission.

title: DIY Dude Replica
tagline: For the artist who wants to sculpt their own... masterpiece. Perfect for that awkward dinner party where someone asks if you’ve ever tried a ‘self-portrait’ in silicone. Comes with everything but the awkward eye contact. Just don’t ask about the shrinkage.

title: Sleepy Time VR
tagline: For the insomniac who wants to pay $2k to dream in 4K, this headset is a godsend. Imagine falling asleep in a meeting, but still technically 'present' in a virtual world.

title: Zippy Aqua Scooter for Grown-Ups
tagline: Forget the jet ski—this is the electric hydrofoil boat your inner child deserves. Perfect for the eco-conscious daredevil who wants to skim across the lake at 30 mph while pretending they're in a sci-fi movie. Just don't blame us when your neighbors mistake you for a low-flying UFO.

title: Tiny Spy in the Sky
tagline: For when you want to document your cat’s 3 AM zoomies without leaving the couch. This nano drone follows your feline’s every move, capturing their midnight escapades in all their chaotic glory. Perfect for the pet parent who’s convinced their cat is plotting something. Just don’t blame us if you start seeing it in your dreams.

title: Sword of Questionable Life Choices
tagline: For that one friend who insists on reenacting Star Wars in feudal Japan, this lightsaber katana is a must. Because what could possibly go wrong with combining two deadly weapons?

title: Isolation Station Luxury
tagline: For when your last 'digital detox' was just deleting Twitter. This island comes with a butler who only speaks in interpretive dance and a chef who thinks 'surprise' is a valid meal plan. Perfect for the trust fund kid who wants to prove they can survive without Uber Eats. Just don't ask about the 'mysterious' extra charges.

title: Cyber Truck for Rebels
tagline: Because your dystopian novel needs a sweet ride, this bulletproof cyber truck is perfect for evading rogue AI or just a really bad traffic jam.

title: Nature's Oddest Journals
tagline: Ever wondered what a platypus' business card looks like? This book is your answer. Perfect for the biology student who needs to impress their professor with 'unique' research material or the dinner party host who wants to ensure no one ever looks them in the eye again.

title: Taco Dream Come True
tagline: Because you clearly need a hotel room that smells like Crunchwrap Supreme, this $169 room is perfect for that one night where you eat an entire Nachos BellGrande by yourself and can't face the judgment of your own bed.

title: Midnight Elixir for the Dramatic
tagline: For when your tap water is too *basic*. Perfect for the goth who wants to 'hydrate in style' or the conspiracy theorist convinced their water is being monitored. Comes in a suspiciously elegant bottle—just don’t ask what’s in it. Ideal for late-night sips while plotting world domination or pretending you’re in a noir film.

title: Space Donut for Your Desk
tagline: Ever needed to explain the Fermi Paradox to your cat while pretending to work? This 3D-printed Ringworld sculpture is your interstellar distraction. It's not just a desk ornament—it's a conversation starter for when your boss asks why you're staring into space (again). Just don't try to fit your coffee in it.

title: Sleepy Time Hoodie
tagline: For when you want to nap at your desk, but still pretend to work, this inflatable sleep hoodie is the answer. Wear it to a meeting to really sell your 'I'm engaged' face.

title: Pixel Perfection in a Pocket
tagline: Remember when your biggest worry was saving Princess Peach? Now you can relive those simpler times with this tiny NES that fits in your pocket. Perfect for those 'I need to prove I was cool in the '80s' moments at family reunions. Just don't expect it to help with your student loans or existential dread.

title: Pyro-Proof Poncho
tagline: For the 'accidental arsonist' who just wanted to grill but somehow set the deck on fire—again. This isn’t your grandma’s apron; it’s a wearable fire blanket for those moments when your flaming kebabs decide to host a barbecue of their own. Perfect for backyard chefs who’ve accepted that their hot dogs will always come with a side of panic.

title: Ol' Blue Eyes' Beach Bungalow
tagline: Ever wanted to host a 'My Way' karaoke night where the walls have literally heard it all? This is your chance. Perfect for the aspiring crooner who needs a beachfront stage with built-in history—just don’t expect the Rat Pack to show up for your luau. Comes with a pool, ocean views, and the lingering ghost of a martini glass clink.

title: Skyward Selfie Stick
tagline: Forget drones—this is the flying phone case you didn’t know you needed. Perfect for when you’re hiking alone and suddenly need to film your own dramatic rescue. Just toss it in the air, and it’ll hover like a nosy helicopter parent, capturing your every move. Bonus: it’ll also judge your life choices from above.

title: Spinal Tap’s Secret Weapon
tagline: For the guitarist who’s convinced their tone is just one click away from perfection. This knob won’t actually improve your playing, but it will make you feel like a rock god when you crank it past 10. Perfect for late-night jam sessions where the neighbors already think you’re in a cult.

title: Ooze Overload: Mutagen Mayhem
tagline: Perfect for when your friend insists on turning their basement into a sewer lair. This TMNT Mutagen Canister Prop Replica is the ideal centerpiece for their 'mad scientist' phase. Just don't blame us if they start sprouting scales or developing a taste for pizza. Comes with a warning label that reads 'Do Not Drink'—because apparently, some people need it spelled out.

title: Busting Spirits, Not Budgets
tagline: Perfect for when your haunted Airbnb has a 'no pets' policy but a very active ghost policy. This proton pack is the only tool that can turn your spectral roommate into a harmless green blob. Just don't ask where you're supposed to store the ectoplasm afterward.

title: Sub or Boat? Why Choose?
tagline: For the aquaphobic yacht enthusiast who wants to sink into the ocean without actually sinking. Perfect for that one friend who insists on 'exploring' every underwater cave during your Caribbean vacation, but also refuses to get their hair wet. Now you can finally say, 'I told you so' when they switch from submarine to speedboat mid-tantrum.

title: Sofa for the Truly Insane
tagline: Because your living room needed a giant gorilla to judge you, this $10k couch is perfect for when you want to reenact King Kong in your apartment, minus the skyscraper.

title: Orchids? More Like Orchid-Not
tagline: For the person who insists their office plant is 'just resting' and not dead. This show is like a TED Talk for your neglected flora—except instead of inspiration, you get a front-row seat to the slow, dramatic death of overpriced greenery. Perfect for the coworker who still hasn’t watered their cactus from 2019.

title: Foosball for Pharaohs
tagline: When your mid-century modern aesthetic just isn’t cutting it, and you need to impress your investment banker friends, this 24K gold foosball table is your golden ticket. Perfect for that awkward moment at your penthouse party when someone asks, 'What do you even do with all that money?' Just reply, 'I play foosball, obviously.'

title: Fancy Farm for Fancy People
tagline: When your 'glamping' budget stretches to 'owning a small country,' this is your starter pack. Perfect for the trust fund baby who wants to 'connect with nature' but still needs a butler to milk the cows. Comes with a 'rustic' barn that's actually more Instagram-friendly than functional. Ideal for hosting a 'farm-to-table' dinner where the 'farm' is your backyard and the 'table' is a $10,000 reclaimed wood slab.

title: Baby Einstein: Derivatives Edition
tagline: Tired of your toddler's 'Why?' phase? Upgrade to 'What's the limit as x approaches infinity?' with this calculus-themed baby book. Perfect for parents who want their kid to either skip kindergarten or develop an existential crisis before potty training. Bonus: Watch them solve for y while you solve for 'why did I buy this?'

title: Smell Like Old Books
tagline: For when you want to reek of a dusty library, but don't have time to actually read. Spray this cologne and instantly transport yourself to a place of mildew and forgotten knowledge.

title: Cap Gun Madness
tagline: For when you need to open a beer and declare war on your neighbor's lawn ornaments at the same time.

title: Scissor Doors, Scissor Prices
tagline: For when your midlife crisis needs a soundtrack of Italian engine roars and the occasional door-scratch on your garage wall. Perfect for the suburban dad who wants to feel like a '80s action hero while picking up groceries. Just remember, the fuel economy is measured in prayers.
